profile.name: Alan B. Bond
profile.bio: Alan B. Bond is a Montclair, New Jersey resident running in NJ-11 under the Hope for Tomorrow label. He holds degrees from Dartmouth and Harvard Business School, worked at Morgan Guaranty, Goldman Sachs and W.R. Lazard, and later ran a pension management firm. He was convicted in a 2003 federal kickback case, served prison time until 2008 and paid restitution and fines.
profile.notes: No published issue positions were found; Ballotpedia could not be retrieved. Instagram account found via search and not opened.

profile.name: Winston Jordan
profile.bio: Winston Jordan is a Brooklyn native living in Hopewell Township, New Jersey. He is a U.S. Army veteran who worked as a computer systems analyst, engineer and IT executive in the pharmaceutical and tech sectors. A former Democrat, he runs an independent campaign that accepts no donations.

platform.point: Pass an American Economic Security Act with a $50,000 minimum livable income guarantee.
Offer a 50-year tax holiday for the bottom 99% of earners.
Run a 24/7 digital town hall letting constituents vote on congressional decisions.
Supports the Stop Act to ban members of Congress from making fundraising calls.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All and a $50,000 guaranteed minimum income.

profile.notes: Campaign site content could not be read in full.

profile.name: Seamus Patrick O'Toole
profile.bio: Seamus Patrick O'Toole is an independent candidate for New Jersey's 7th congressional district, appearing on the ballot under the slogan "Stop Israel's Genocide." He qualified by petition, and his signatures withstood a challenge in June 2026.

platform.point: Runs on a ballot slogan centred on opposing Israel's military conduct in Gaza.

profile.notes: No campaign website, biography or detailed positions were found beyond the ballot slogan.

profile.name: Aristotle Eliopoulos
profile.bio: Aristotle "Ari" Eliopoulos is a teacher and union representative running as an independent in New Jersey's 8th congressional district, with the backing of three Republican county chairs. He was raised in Jersey City by Greek immigrant parents who ran a small business.

platform.point: Wants to address underfunded classrooms in public schools.
Pledges to tackle rising costs facing working families.
Aims to remove barriers for children with disabilities.

education.evidence: Campaign highlights underfunded public school classrooms as a core issue.

profile.notes: His campaign site publishes only brief issue themes; the headshot on the site is embedded inline rather than as a linkable image URL.

profile.name: Craig Honts
profile.bio: Craig Honts is the Socialist Workers Party candidate for New Jersey's 8th congressional district. He was the party's nominee for lieutenant governor of New Jersey in 2025, running with gubernatorial candidate Joanne Kuniansky.
profile.notes: No campaign website or candidate-specific statements were found; positions were not inferred from the party label.
